newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks set records as dollar surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks set records as dollar surges.

text.p: Leading European stock markets closed at record levels on Friday as Wall Street recovered from an uncertain start and the dollar powered to a 30-month high against the mark.
Shares in London and Frankfurt broke through psychological barriers in early trade and weathered mid-afternoon doubts before ending close to their trading peaks after a week of record breaking.
Paris also set records, closing just below its all-time intraday high with dealers likewise citing the dollar, which was helped along by favourable trade data.

In London, the FTSE index burst through 4,200 points as dealers heaved a sigh of relief that finance minister Kenneth Clarke had decided against the interest rate rise which the Bank of England has long been seeking.
Later enthusiasm started to flag as Wall Street opened indecisively following its record close on Thursday.
But the FTSE picked up when U.S. stocks gained momentum and it closed 10.2 points up at 4,207.7, its third record close of the week, leaving it 151.1 points or 3.7 percent up on last Friday's close.
Analysts said shares could come off the boil in the short term, but with Wall Street continuing to make progress, the outlook for London was bright.
"The FTSE is slightly overbought short-term but it is still looking bullish," said Richard Marshall, an director at Investment Research of Cambridge, a specialist research house.
"After a bit of consolidation it is looking likely to move on to 4,300, which is the next round figure."
Dealers in continental European markets also looked to the Dow, which was at 6,797.31 in afternoon trade, 31.94 points higher than Thursday's record close.
In Frankfurt, the DAX breached the 3,000 point barrier for the first time to close up 8.06 points at a record 3,001.37.
But German dealers took the excitement in their stride. "Of course we are happy to see the 3,000 mark but it doesn't mean the start of anything big," said one dealer.
French shares continued the bull run which began on January 2 and the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.33 points at 2,425.10 after nudging an all time high at 2,426.13.
"The market wants to rise. New York is busy breaking new records and so are we," a trader said. "There is a lot of volume, loads of cash is being invested and that is going to continue."

Behind the week of records lay the dollar, which was particularly encouraging for German exporters. It powered to its highest level since June 1994 after U.S. trade data gave it the ammunition to breach stiff resistance levels.
The November trade deficit was $8.40 billion, widening from $8.01 billion in the previous month. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a deficit of 9.8 billion dollars.
The dollar sailed through technical barriers to the day's high of 1.6125 marks after the trade figures, up from 1.5957 at the European close on Thursday.
"The weak mark has been the driving force behind the dollar's rally, and the trade data gave it even more impetus," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 117.26 yen and 1.6135 marks, compared with 116.53 and 1.5945 late on Thursday.
Sterling firmed to 2.6920 marks from 2.6745 late on Thursday. The French franc eased to 3.3723 marks from 3.3748.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares closed 10.2 higher at 4,207.7, the first time it has gone through 4,200.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index broke through 3,000 before closing up 8.06 at 3,001.37 points.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed up 17.33 at 2,425.10 also above Thursday's record close of 2,407.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $355.15, up from Thursday's close of $353.35. Silver was slightly stronger at $4.77, up six cents from the previous London close.
